disposition_reason: Retail survey of 164 packaged dried mushrooms (six species, eight Polish producers) bought January-June 2025, analysed for cadmium, lead, total mercury and arsenic; medians, quartiles and ranges by product type, species and producer in Tables 2-5.

study.design: Cross-sectional retail survey of packaged dried mushrooms
study.origin: Declared origin: Poland 66%, EU/non-EU unspecified 24%, unclear 10%; 2024 harvest (90%) and 2023 harvest (10%)
study.market: Retail outlets in Poland, products of eight Polish producers
study.method: Microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion; Cd and Pb by ET-AAS, total Hg by CV-AFS, As by ICP-OES
study.lod_text: LOQ Cd 0.01, Pb 0.10, As 0.66, Hg 0.002 mg/kg; LOD Cd 0.005, Pb 0.05, As 0.27, Hg 0.001 mg/kg; <LOQ substituted with half LOQ
study.qa: Spike recoveries (Table S5, supplement not available); certified calibration solutions

controls.control: Certified organic (ecological) product versus conventional wild-growing product
controls.outcome: Mercury median 0.029 (organic) vs 0.070 mg/kg (conventional), p=0.007; arsenic median below LOQ vs 1.232 mg/kg, p=0.0002; cadmium 0.95 vs 0.52 and lead both below LOQ, not significant
Mercury medians ranged 0.019 to 0.825 mg/kg and cadmium medians 0.09 to 1.475 mg/kg across producers, with significant Kruskal-Wallis differences
Button mushroom lowest (Cd median 0.040, Hg 0.001 substitute); porcini highest Cd (1.30) and Hg (0.243); slippery jack highest As (5.364 mg/kg)
